newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks set record close, look to Budget.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks set record close, look to Budget.

text.p: The Australian share market set closing and intraday record highs on Tuesday, taking its cue from another record run on Wall Street.

The All Ordinaries index added 9.5 points to close at 2,534.3, surpassing the previous record closing high of 2,526.0 set on May 9. The benchmark index also registered a new intraday high of 2,540.4, toppling Monday's record of 2,538.0.
An optimistic market locked in most of the early gains as pre-Budget nerves seemed to be calmed by the overall firm tone that was evident. The Federal budget is due this evening.

"Our market has been good and I think it will continue that way," said broker Kevin Lourey of Peake Lands Kirwan, adding that while it was the current event of note, he was not expecting dramatic things from the 1997/98 fiscal programme.
"I think the budget will be pretty benign. I don't think there will be any earth shattering news coming out of it."
Others agreed, saying traders had factored in a budget broadly favourable to financial markets.
"Everyone seems to expect a reasonably favourable result. Generally I don't think it is going to impact too greatly on our market," said a dealer at a Melbourne-based investment house.
Banks led the way to higher ground with half year profit expectations fueling three of the big four banks.

Westpac Banking Corp, which reports on Wednesday, was up eight cents to A$7.50 (US$5.85) while sector leader National Australia Bank, due to report on Thursday, edged its way to another record high at A$18.35 before ending up 15.7 cents at A$18.337. ANZ Bank, which is due to report next week, climbed nine cents to A$8.49.
Oil/gas major Woodside Petroleum added 16 cents to end at A$10.86 after oil prices jumped offshore.

On the negative side, key industrials CSR Ltd and Amcor Ltd featured. CSR shares lost 13.3 cents to A$4.63 after the building materials, sugar and aluminium group reported a slump in full year net profit to A$212.2 million on Monday.

Sellers savaged paper and packaging giant Amcor after it issued a warning on second half profits, saying trading conditions remained difficult. Amcor was at a nine month high of A$8.75 prior to the warning but ended 18 cents down at A$8.45 on turnover of 2.5 million shares.
Rises outnumbered falls by a ratio of about seven to five, while about 31 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
